SMTO-UI-0052 — This page needs to reload

GUID: 79fdf1df-bf1d-51da-8538-8ad4cd9f75a9
Slug: ui-page-stale
Domain: UI · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The SMTO server was updated after you opened this page, so the page is out of date and can't show the new memory indexing progress. Reloading the page fixes this.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Copy any text you've typed but not sent. Reloading the page clears unsent text.
  2. Select Reload this page in this message, or use your browser's reload button. Reloading loads the newer version of SMTO's pages from the updated server.
  3. If the message comes back, reload while skipping the browser's saved copy: press Ctrl+Shift+R (on a Mac, Cmd+Shift+R). Your browser may be reusing an old saved copy of the page instead of fetching the new one.

What success looks like

  • Memory indexing progress appears without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and open System Health to see whether the server reports any other problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • This page needs to reload.

What this means

  • The running server advertises a newer interface than this page knows how to display. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported ui_page_stale. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The reloaded page accepts the current response.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • running_capabilities reports knowledge.memory_index at a revision newer than this page supports, so the browser is running old UI assets. Reload the page (a hard reload if assets are cached); if it persists, check that the static assets served match the running Server build.
  • Keep any unsaved text, then reload this page to use the current server interface.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reloaded page accepts the current response.

How to verify the fix

  • The reloaded page accepts the current response.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
